content:
A Blinkit delivery guy asked me a simple question — and it completely changed how I see brands like Zepto, Zomato and Swiggy
A few days ago, while receiving a Blinkit order, the delivery guy casually asked me:
“How do you know Blinkit? Most people only know Zepto. Very few know Blinkit.”
That question stayed in my head.
Because he was right.
In most people’s minds:
> Zepto, Blinkit, Instamart = three different companies.
And Zepto is the most “famous” one.
Later that day, I discovered something that genuinely shocked me.
Blinkit is actually owned by Zomato.
And that’s when the real learning started.
Swiggy vs Zomato — very different brand strategy
Everyone knows:
> Swiggy → Instamart
Because:
Same app
Same colors
Same logo
Same delivery experience
Your brain stores it as one brand.
But with Zomato:
Zomato is red
Blinkit is yellow
Separate app
Separate identity
No loud “by Zomato” anywhere
So your brain stores it as two companies.
Even though they belong to the same parent (now called Eternal Ltd).
---
Why this is genius
This is called a House of Brands strategy.
The idea is:
> Let each brand live independently in the customer’s mind.
So:
If Blinkit fails → Zomato image is safe
If Zomato has issues → Blinkit is safe
Both can compete without being tied emotionally
Swiggy uses a Branded House (everything is Swiggy).
Zomato/Eternal uses a House of Brands (separate identities).
---
Then I noticed something even crazier
This exact strategy is what Tata has been doing for 100+ years.
You don’t think:
“Tata clothes” → you think Westside, Zudio
“Tata jewellery” → you think Tanishq
“Tata electronics” → you think Croma
“Tata groceries” → you think BigBasket
“Tata hotels” → you think Taj
“Tata tea” → you think Tata Tea, Tetley
“Tata cars” → you think Nexon, Punch
You can live an entire day using Tata products and never feel like you used a Tata product.
That’s elite branding.
And suddenly Blinkit made sense to me.
---
Why Zepto feels more famous than Blinkit (even though Blinkit is older)
Blinkit started in 2013 as Grofers.
Zepto started only in 2021.
But Zepto feels bigger in people’s minds because:
It was born as “10-minute delivery”
Strong founder story
Sharp name
Aggressive marketing during the quick commerce boom
Purple bags everywhere
Blinkit had to rebrand from an old image. Zepto came fresh.
Timing + storytelling > history.
---
My learning from all this
Branding is not about ownership.
Branding is about what people remember.
People remember:
Zepto as a startup
Instamart as Swiggy
Blinkit as independent
Even when reality is different.
And that invisibility?
That’s by design.
---
Final thought
We often think companies compete only in operations.
But they are actually competing in how your brain categorizes them.
And once you see this, you start noticing it everywhere — especially with Tata.
All because a Blinkit delivery guy asked me one innocent question.

I don’t use those. I like to pick out my own groceries, particularly anything perishable, and it’s more hassle to wait downstairs in the lobby to wait for the delivery. For the “curbside pickup” I still don’t trust the store’s judgment on my produce and don’t want my milk sitting around waiting for me to come get it.

Do you do yoga, mindfulness or urban hiking? Shopping is my time, to be centered. The mind is on auto-pilot. What you want? What do you need more of? What will be good today? Tomorrow? Feeding three lives, what is best for them, us or me? Is this my religion? Is this becoming a sacred ritual: holy Shopping? The sacrament of Purchase! Maybe, it’s psychological? Supplying a need. I enter, surrender to the senses, shop, buy, prepare, consume. Repeat as necessary. No thinking involved and yet, it is nothing but thinking, in a spiritual way, if you want. A public market is like a mass in a cathedral or a Southern Baptist Sunday service. Existing somewhere else, that’s just not right here!! I will always shop. There is no change.

Experts say that earlier customers preferred to shop online for groceries based on factors like convenience and affordability. But now somewhere shopping for groceries online has become a necessity for some due to the pandemic and a safe shopping option for others. On the other hand, to enjoy the growth in the online grocery delivery market several offline grocery retailers have shifted online to serve their customers more conveniently. I think that the future belongs to online shopping because it is more comfortable and convenient.
